Chlorine was first added to a public drinking water supply in 1897 in Maidstone, England, when the town’s entire water supply was treated with chlorine [d1,d2]. In the United States, continuous chlorination began in 1908 at Jersey City, New Jersey’s Boonton Reservoir, marking the first routine use of chlorine to disinfect U.S. tap water [d5,d7,d9]. These accounts are complementary: the 1897 event refers to the first town-wide chlorination in England, while the 1908 milestone refers to the first continuous U.S. system [d2,d5,d7].
